specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** formative-summative-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of ten assessment activities as formative or summative by its purpose, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** The Practice Metric, Formative Assessment (both defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each activity the learner commits one of two bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A quiz is always formative. (2) Formative assessment never involves a grade. (3) Summative assessment is more important than formative assessment. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying by purpose is an Understand-level action. Ten activities in which the format is the same but the purpose differs teach the learner to ask what the result is used for. **Content:** The two bins: Formative (used during learning to guide the next step) and Summative (used at the end to judge what was learned). The ten activities: | # | Activity shown to the learner | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A three-question ungraded check at the end of a lesson, with answers shown at once. | Formative | It helps learners see what they know now. | | 2 | A final exam that sets the course grade. | Summative | It judges what was learned at the end. | | 3 | A teacher asks learners to hold up cards with their answer to a question in the middle of a lesson. | Formative | It tells the teacher what to do next. | | 4 | A state test given at the end of the school year. | Summative | It judges what was learned over the year. | | 5 | A draft essay returned with comments and no grade. | Formative | It guides the next draft. | | 6 | A unit test that counts toward the report card. | Summative | It judges what was learned in the unit. | | 7 | A self-check quiz in a chapter that lets learners retry. | Formative | It supports practice and can be repeated. | | 8 | A capstone project graded against a rubric at the end of a program. | Summative | It judges final achievement. | | 9 | An exit ticket that asks learners to name one thing they are still unsure about. | Formative | It shows what to teach next. | | 10 | A certificate exam that decides whether a learner passes. | Summative | It decides an outcome. | **Provenance:** The activities are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The definitions follow the chapter section "Formative Assessment". **Rules:** Each activity has exactly one correct bin, five per bin. The bin depends on how the result is used. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one activity and the two bins. 2. The learner places the activity in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After activity 10 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 10 activities in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt". At 9 or more it adds "You can tell assessment for learning from assessment of learning." Below 9 it lists the Why text of each missed activity. **Starting State:** The first activity and two empty bins. The question shown is "Is this used during learning or at the end?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says formative assessment guides learning and is low stakes, and summative assessment judges what was learned at the end.
